rounds.text: Raymond Realty Ltd trades at an exceptionally low P/E ratio of 8.27x against a sector benchmark of 57.67x, while delivering stellar profitability with an ROE of 37.02% and an ROCE of 29.99% that dwarf sector medians [E6, E9, E10]. Intrinsic value calculations via discounted cash flow place the fair value significantly above the current market price of ₹ 658, leaving a massive margin of safety of 59.1% [E2, E32, E33]. The reverse DCF model confirms that the current market price implies a paltry 5.7% earnings growth, which stands in stark contrast to the base case assumption of 18.0% and the company's historical compounded profit growth [E14, E34]. Management provides robust forward guidance of a minimum 20% growth on pre-sales and top-line for FY27, underpinned by advanced project pipelines in Mahim and a growing JDA portfolio boasting a revenue potential of approximately INR 17,000 crores [E59, E60, E67]. Conceded: operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative at ₹ -145 Cr, resulting in a weak cash conversion of -0.55x and rising borrowings [E21, E22, E26]. Promoter confidence remains high, however, with insider holdings increasing by 2.06 percentage points to 50.93% in June 2026 [E28].

The most glaring risk in Raymond Realty Ltd is the complete collapse of its cash generation, evidenced by operating cash flow crashing to Rs -145 Cr and free cash flow plunging to Rs -193 Cr in Mar 2026 [E22, E23]. This creates a severe cash conversion ratio of -0.55x against reported profit, meaning operating cash flow represents a negative 27% of operating profit [E21, E24]. Consequently, borrowings have surged from Rs 0 Cr to Rs 661 Cr in a single year, driving debt to equity to 0.43x [E25, E26]. Furthermore, reported earnings are flattered by Rs 110 Cr of other income, masking the underlying cash deterioration [E47]. Institutional confidence is evaporating rapidly, with foreign institutional holdings plunging from 15.52% to 5.85% and domestic institutions cutting stakes from 6.35% to 2.90% in just one year, triggering a negative money flow signal [E29, E30, E31]. Conceded: the company boasts an impressive ROCE of 33.8% and high trailing profit growth [E12, E15]. Despite these high headline returns, the stock suffers from extreme volatility of 65.3% and a negative Sharpe ratio of -0.19, alongside a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -63.1% [E40, E41, E42].

Conceded: operating cash flow dropped to Rs -145 Cr and free cash flow reached Rs -193 Cr in Mar 2026 [E22, E23]. However, this cash burn occurs while scaling rapidly within a steady MMR market where actual user demand prioritizes trusted developers, supporting management's minimum 20% growth guidance for pre-sales and top-line in FY27 [E59, E62, E64]. The resulting gross debt-to-equity ratio of 0.6 remains comfortably below the company's internal ceiling of 1:1, backed by a fully funded liquidity buffer of INR358 crores for the upcoming year [E69, E70]. While foreign and domestic institutional holdings declined over the year [E29, E30], promoters increased their stake by 2.06 percentage points to 50.93% as of Jun 2026, demonstrating strong internal conviction [E28]. Furthermore, the company maintains a robust seven-project JDA portfolio with a massive revenue potential of approximately INR17,000 crores alongside advanced approval stages for upcoming launches in Mahim and Thane [E60, E67, E71, E72]. Finally, historical volatility and drawdowns [E40, E41] are outweighed by exceptional fundamentals, including an ROCE of 33.8% and an ROE of 32.6% [E12, E13].

However, dismissing institutional flight as "decoupled" ignores a massive stampede where foreign institutions slashed holdings by 9.67 percentage points and domestic institutions cut by 3.45 percentage points, registering negative money flow [E29, E30, E31]. Conceded: gross debt-to-equity is 0.6 and a liquidity buffer of INR358 crores exists [E69, E70]. Yet brushing off negative operating cash flow of Rs -145 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -193 Cr as mere "scaling" minimizes severe cash burn, where cash conversion plummeted to -0.55x against reported profit [E21, E22, E23]. Conceded: borrowings were deployed while managing a JDA pipeline and targeting 20% growth [E59, E67]. Nonetheless, debt surged from zero to Rs 661 Cr in a single year, introducing a brand-new leverage risk that did not exist previously [E26]. Finally, the bull minimizes Rs 110 Cr in other income, but when earnings contain non-operating inflows alongside inconsistent quarterly operating margins, reported profitability requires heavy scrutiny [E47, E20].

evidence.quote: So, construction cost impact will actually play out over the longer period of time. If it dies out in the next two months or three months, you will not even see that kind of impact. But the absorption capacity for that cost increase is there in the market and we will pass it on.
